chunks: Ibn Abi al-Bilad, from one who informed him, from some of the jurists, who said:

The poor of the believers will be stopped [before God] on the Day of Resurrection, and the Lord, Blessed and Exalted, will say to them: 'Verily, I did not impoverish you because of your insignificance to Me, but I impoverished you to test you. Go forth, and no one who did you a favor in the world shall remain [unavenged]; you shall take his hand and bring him into Paradise.'

key_terms.صَنَعَ إِلَيْكُمْ مَعْرُوفًا: Did you a favor / conferred a benefit upon you

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the poor believers' status on the Day of Resurrection according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, God reassures the poor believers that their destitution was a deliberate trial (*ibtila*) to elevate their status, not a consequence of divine neglect. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual merit of the *Fuqara*, granting them the unique privilege of personally escorting their benefactors into Paradise, thereby transforming social debt into eternal reward.
